problem: Given that $X∼B(7,0.5),$ compute $P(X\le 6).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.

feedback.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(12,\frac{2}{3}),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{12}{x}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{x}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{12-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X\le 11)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,…,11.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X>11)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=12,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X>11),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>11) & =P(X\in {12}) \\  & =f(12) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{12}{12}){(\frac{2}{3})}^{12}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{12-12} \\  & =1{(\frac{2}{3})}^{12}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{0} \\  & ≈0.008\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 11) & =1-P(X>11) \\  & ≈1-0.008 \\  & =0.992\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
